title: Functional expression of engineered IsPETase and LCC variants in Drosophila melanogaster reveals host tolerance and differential catalytic activity.
abstract: Insects offer promising opportunities for organic waste bioconversion; however, they cannot efficiently degrade synthetic polymers such as polyethylene terephthalate (PET). Here, we generated transgenic Drosophila melanogaster lines to express in vitro-evolved variants of two PET-degrading enzymes with distinct biochemical properties: an engineered Ideonella sakaiensis PETase variant (TS-ΔIsPET) and a leaf-branch compost cutinase variant (TA-ΔLCC). Both enzymes, fused to a Drosophila gut-derived secretory signal, were produced and secreted by Drosophila cultured S2R+ cells and transgenic larvae. Upon secretion, TS-ΔIsPET and TA-ΔLCC enzymes were glycosylated, a post-translational modification that did not abolish their catalytic activity. Notably, TA-ΔLCC displayed ∼6-fold higher net esterase activity than TS-ΔIsPET in larval samples, and TA-ΔLCC-containing extracts depolymerised PET nanoparticles in vitro under enzyme-favourable conditions. Transgenic flies showed normal development, fertility and survival. Morphological and biochemical analyses confirmed that TA-ΔLCC expression did not alter midgut structure and function. Together, these results establish Drosophila melanogaster as a model for functional expression and comparative evaluation of engineered PET-degrading enzymes and identify TA-ΔLCC as a promising candidate for further evaluation in insect species relevant to plastic-contaminated waste bioconversion.

title: Species-specific digestive enzyme profiles reveal trophodynamic differences between blue mussels and their endoparasitic copepods but limited responses to feeding, starvation, and microplastic exposure.
journal: Comp Biochem Physiol B Biochem Mol Biol (2026)
abstract: Blue mussels (Mytilus edulis) from the southern North Sea are exposed to multiple natural and anthropogenic stressors, including parasite infestation and microplastic pollution. For example, the intestinal copepods Mytilicola intestinalis and Mytilicola orientalis are common endoparasites of blue mussels in the coastal areas. We investigated the prevalence and composition of Mytilicola species in mussels from the Wadden Sea. The infestation rate of M. edulis by Mytilicola spp. was 78%. One third of infested mussels harboured both parasite species. These parasites may feed on intestinal tissue, detached cells, or the gut content of the host which also may contain natural and anthropogenic microparticles that were ingested by the mussel. In a 5-day laboratory experiment, mussels either received no food, were fed with microalgae, or were exposed to microplastics. Activities of selected digestive enzymes were measured in the midgut gland of the mussels and in whole parasites. Digestive enzyme profiles revealed significant functional differences between the host and either parasite. Mussels showed high esterase and β-glucosidase activities, reflecting the utilization of algal food. In contrast, both Mytilicola species showed low β-glucosidase activities. Elevated α-glucosidase and N-acetyl-β-D-glucosaminidase activities in M. orientalis suggest the utilization of glycogen and mucus from the host. Treatments involving starvation, feeding, and microplastics had no significant effects on the enzyme profiles of the host, and there was no correlation between the enzyme activities of the host and its parasites. Enzyme profiles proved useful for interpreting trophodynamic interactions between mussels and their Mytilicola endoparasites, but there were limited responses to exposure conditions for all species.

title: Radiolabelled cyclodextrins to detect cervical cancer: a preclinical feasibility study.
abstract: Radiolabelled cyclodextrins targeting prostaglandin E2 (PGE2) seem promising candidates for positron emission tomography (PET)-based molecular imaging of cervical cancer. Here, we evaluated the performance of gallium-68-labelled 2-hydroxypropyl-β-cyclodextrin (HPβCD) and randomly methylated β-cyclodextrin (RAMEB) for the in vivo PET detection of cervical cancer. P-glycoprotein positive (Pgp+) KB-V-1 and P-glycoprotein negative (Pgp-) KB-3-1 cervical carcinoma xenografts of varying sizes (small-, medium-, large-sized) were established and subjected to [68Ga]Ga-NODAGA-HPβCD and [68Ga]Ga-DOTAGA-RAMEB PET imaging followed by ex vivo biodistribution and immunohistochemical (IHC) analysis of PGE2 and Pgp expression. In line with the IHC results, PET data revealed the capability of both radiotracers to reliably detect each tumor types independent of tumor size. Nevertheless, the modest increase in uptake observed with increasing size may indicate enhanced tumor aggressiveness and angiogenic activity. Comparable radiotracer accumulation in MDR-positive and MDR-negative tumors suggests that HPβCD and RAMEB derivatives are unlikely to serve as substrates of Pgp enabling tumor detection across different tumor types. Collectively, our findings demonstrate that radiolabelled cyclodextrins are promising PET tracers for the in vivo detection of cervical cancer, irrespective of tumor size and Pgp expression.

title: Evaluating [18F]-AlF-FAPI-74 PET/CT for diagnosis of the unfavourable CMS4 colorectal cancer subtype (FoCus study): protocol for a prospective, observational, proof-of-concept clinical study.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Consensus molecular subtype 4 (CMS4) colorectal cancer (CRC) is characterised by stromal activation, therapy resistance and poor prognosis. Current CMS4 assessment relies on tissue sampling, which is limited by sampling bias due to inter-lesion and intra-lesion heterogeneity. Fibroblast activation protein (FAP) gene-expression is strongly associated with CMS4 status. [18F]-AlF-FAPI-74 positron emission tomography (PET)/ computed tomography (CT) enables non-invasive, whole-body assessment of FAP expression and may therefore provide an imaging-based biomarker for CMS4 status in CRC. METHODS AND ANALYSIS: FoCus is a prospective, observational proof-of-concept clinical study including 45 patients (≥18 years) with resectable metachronous or synchronous colorectal liver metastases. Eligible patients must have at least one liver metastasis of ≥15 mm scheduled for surgical resection. Patients will undergo [18F]-AlF-FAPI-74 PET/CT prior to clinically indicated therapeutic interventions, including surgical resection of primary tumours and/or metastases and, when applicable, prior to systemic therapy. The primary endpoint is CMS4 status, determined by RNA sequencing of resected tumour tissue using multi-region sampling to account for spatial heterogeneity. Diagnostic performance of FAPI-PET (index test) for CMS4 classification (reference standard) will be evaluated using receiver operating characteristic analysis at the tumour-level. Secondary endpoints include FAP expression assessed by immunohistochemistry and ELISA. ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION: The study has been approved by the institutional review board NedMec+, the Netherlands (protocol 23-298; Clinical Trials Information System EU CT number: 2023-509183-17-00). All participants will provide written informed consent. Results will be disseminated through peer-reviewed publications and scientific conferences. TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: NCT06191120.

title: De Novo Design of a TROP-2-Targeting Peptide PET Tracer via AI-Guided Binding Interface Mimicry.
mesh: Humans; Animals; Antigens, Neoplasm; Cell Adhesion Molecules; Mice; Peptides; Cell Line, Tumor; Tissue Distribution; Male; Gallium Radioisotopes; Positron Emission Tomography Computed Tomography; Positron-Emission Tomography; Drug Design; Molecular Mimicry; Mice, Nude; Radiopharmaceuticals
abstract: Trophoblast cell surface antigen 2 (TROP-2) is a transmembrane glycoprotein overexpressed across a range of epithelial malignancies, yet its clinical assessment still relies largely on invasive immunohistochemical analysis of biopsied tissues. In this study, we employed the PepMimic artificial intelligence platform to de novo design a TROP-2-targeting peptide, TR23, via binding interface mimicry, which was subsequently conjugated with DOTA and radiolabeled with 68Ga to yield the peptide-based PET probe [68Ga]Ga-DOTA-TR23. The tracer bound TROP-2 with nanomolar affinity (KD = 26.8 nM), showed selective cellular uptake in TROP-2-positive cells, and exhibited high radiochemical purity (>95%) with excellent stability in saline and serum. Micro-PET/CT imaging in pancreatic (BxPC-3), prostate (PC3), and thyroid (BCPAP) xenograft models revealed rapid, specific tumor accumulation with high contrast and low background uptake, while competitive blocking studies with excess unlabeled TR23 substantially suppressed tumor uptake, confirming receptor-mediated specificity. Quantitative analysis further demonstrated strong positive correlations between SUVmax and TROP-2 expression levels verified by immunohistochemistry across all three tumor types. Collectively, these findings establish [68Ga]Ga-DOTA-TR23 as a promising peptide-based PET tracer for rapid, specific, and quantitative imaging of TROP-2-positive tumors, and highlight the PepMimic-enabled strategy as a versatile platform for peptide-based probe discovery, supporting the translational potential of this tracer as a pan-cancer diagnostic agent for precision molecular imaging.

title: B7-H3 molecular imaging for the era of pan-cancer targeted therapy.
abstract: B7-H3 (CD276) is broadly overexpressed across solid tumors and plays active roles in immune evasion, tumor angiogenesis, and metabolic reprogramming. As B7-H3-directed antibody-drug conjugates chimeric antigen receptor T-cell therapies, and radioimmunotherapy agents advance through clinical trials, non-invasive whole-body imaging of B7-H3 expression has become a pressing clinical need. Tissue biopsy with IHC cannot capture systemic target heterogeneity, and the recent IDeate-PanTumor01 trial found no correlation between baseline B7-H3 H-score and response to ifinatamab deruxtecan-illustrating the gap that molecular imaging must fill. This mini review surveys B7-H3-targeted imaging agents by scaffold class-antibodies, affibodies, nanobodies, and bicyclic peptides-and examines radioimmunotherapy platforms that couple PET-based dosimetry with targeted radionuclide delivery.

title: Newly diagnosed and relapsed follicular lymphoma: EHA Clinical Practice Guidelines for diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up.
abstract: Follicular lymphoma (FL) is the second most common lymphoma subtype in Europe, with a median age at diagnosis of 60-65 years. It is generally considered an indolent disease, and the median overall survival at diagnosis now likely exceeds 20 years. However, considerable heterogeneity exists. Diagnosis requires adequate biopsy material and a specialized hematopathologist. Staging and prognosis rely on positron emission tomography (PET)-computed tomography (CT). Prognostication at diagnosis is based on several validated clinical prognostic scores. Localized disease is usually treated with radiotherapy ± Rituximab. The treatment of disseminated disease includes active surveillance (or in selected cases Rituximab monotherapy) for low-tumor burden patients, and most often immunochemotherapy (or in selected cases chemo-free therapeutic options), ±antibody maintenance in high-tumor burden patients. For relapsed or refractory disease, treatment with Rituximab-Lenalidomide combination ± Tafasitamab or Epcoritamab from the first relapse and single-agent bispecific antibodies, chimeric antigen receptor T-cell therapy (CAR-T) cells, and Zanubrutinib-Obinutuzumab after second relapse should be prioritized over immunochemotherapy. Given the long natural history and risk of relapse, careful follow-up is an important part of patient management. Patients should be actively involved in decision-making. In this guideline, we present current evidence-based recommendations for diagnosis, staging, treatment, and follow-up.

title: Merkel Cell Carcinoma Masquerading as Dermatitis.
abstract: Merkel cell carcinoma (MCC) is a rare, highly aggressive neuroendocrine skin carcinoma that typically presents as a rapidly enlarging, firm, painless nodule on sun-exposed areas in elderly patients. This malignancy is characterized by high rates of local recurrence, regional spread, and distant metastasis. We report a case of a woman in her 80s who presented with an erythematous patch on the left anterior thigh, a non-sun-exposed site, initially diagnosed as inflammatory dermatitis and treated with topical corticosteroids. After two months of failed therapy and interval growth, a punch biopsy was performed. Histopathology revealed a dermal infiltrate of small to medium-sized cells with "salt and pepper" chromatin and numerous mitotic figures. Immunohistochemistry confirmed a diagnosis of MCC. Staging with positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) revealed an incidental pancreatic lesion with benign cytology and subsequent imaging stability but no evidence of metastatic disease. The staging workup was complicated by acute pancreatitis for which she was hospitalized, and during which she developed new-onset atrial fibrillation and congestive heart failure. After discharge, the patient underwent wide local excision; however, sentinel lymph node biopsy was deferred due to the patient's acute comorbidities. In conjunction with the patient, the decision was made for close surveillance rather than adjuvant radiation or systemic therapy. At the most recent follow-up, 16 months after excision, there was no evidence of recurrence. This case highlights an atypical presentation of MCC as a dermatitic-appearing patch in a non-sun-exposed area and underscores the importance of biopsy in atypical lesions that do not respond to treatment, as well as the need to individualize treatment in elderly patients with significant competing comorbidities.

title: 12-Month Disease-Free Survival Prediction in Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma: A Multimodal Transfer Learning Innovation.
journal: Proc SPIE Int Soc Opt Eng (2026)
abstract: Early relapse of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) within 12 months of diagnosis confers a poor prognosis, underscoring the critical need for accurate pretreatment prediction. Current approaches relying on radiomics and clinical indicators are limited by scarce medical imaging data, time-consuming manual feature extraction (susceptible to human subjectivity), and insufficient use of multimodal deep learning frameworks. To address these challenges, we propose MM-DLBCL, a novel multimodal transfer learning framework for pretreatment 12-month disease-free survival (DFS12) prediction. It leverages the biomedical pre-trained PMC-CLIP model to mitigate small-sample constraints, uses pretreatment FDG-PET/CT scans to generate coronal and sagittal Maximum Intensity Projection (MIP) images (focusing on metabolically active lesions), and converts key clinical covariates (e.g., International Prognostic Index (IPI) score, disease stage, serum lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) levels) into structured text embeddings. The architecture integrates an enhanced ResNet50 visual encoder (for dual-plane MIP feature extraction), a PubMedBERT text encoder (for clinical data processing), a Medical-Statistical Feature Fusion (MSFF) module (to quantify tumor heterogeneity via higher-order statistics), a Multi-Scaled Cooperative Attention (MSCA) module (to align imaging and clinical features), and a Cross-Modal Contrastive Head (CMCH) module (to optimize discriminative power via triple contrastive loss). Trained and validated on a retrospective cohort of 338 DLBCL adult patients, MM-DLBCL achieved an end-to-end AUC of 0.8316 ± 0.06 and accuracy of 0.8044 ± 0.05 for DFS12 prediction, demonstrating significant potential for multimodal transfer learning in automated DLBCL disease-free survival risk stratification.

title: Intelligent immunotherapy: AI-driven optimization of CAR-T therapy in hematologic malignancies.
abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T cell therapy has transformed outcomes in selected hematologic malignancies, yet its delivery remains constrained by variable efficacy, acute and prolonged toxicities, and complex manufacturing logistics. Artificial intelligence (AI) is being applied across the CAR-T continuum at three distinct levels of evidentiary maturity. Externally validated parsimonious models built on routine clinical and laboratory data including CAR-HEMATOTOX, endothelial activation and stress index (EASIX) and m-EASIX, MyCARe, and gradient-boosting cytokine release syndrome predictors provide deployable risk stratification today. Methodologically sophisticated tools using deep-learning positron emission tomography (PET) segmentation, attention-based digital-pathology analysis, and multimodal fusion of imaging with laboratory and circulating tumor DNA features have demonstrated technical promise but generally lack the multi-center external validation required for clinical-grade deployment. Forward-looking applications, including digital-twin frameworks, large language models, and closed-loop adaptive therapy, remain at the prototype stage and have not yet been validated for CAR-T. This review synthesizes these three tiers, summarizes 18 published AI and statistical-modeling tools in a comparative performance table, and compares data characteristics and AI modeling paradigms across large B cell lymphoma, B cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia, and multiple myeloma. We also identify the implementation realities-absent regulatory clearance, demographic and racial bias in training data, and post-deployment model drift-that condition the field's evolution. The contribution of AI to CAR-T therapy, as the evidence currently stands, is the calibrated quantification of established risk factors rather than the discovery of novel biology, but the methodological and data infrastructure foundations are now in place for the broader transformation that the next decade may enable.

title: EGFR-mutated lung adenocarcinoma presenting as miliary intrapulmonary carcinomatosis: A diagnostic mimic of tuberculosis.
abstract: Miliary intrapulmonary carcinomatosis (MIPC) is a rare metastatic pattern of lung cancer that closely mimics disseminated tuberculosis (TB), posing a significant diagnostic challenge. We present a 53-year-old Filipino woman, a lifelong nonsmoker with prior latent TB, who presented with progressive cough and a diffuse bilateral miliary nodular pattern on chest imaging. An extensive infectious workup was unrevealing, and bronchoscopic biopsy revealed poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma (TTF-1+) harboring an EGFR exon 21 L858R mutation. Staging demonstrated brain, osseous, and pleural metastases (stage IVB NSCLC). The patient was initiated on osimertinib 80 mg daily with palliative radiation and zoledronic acid, achieving no evidence of active disease at 2.5 years on serial PET-CT and brain MRI. This case underscores the importance of tissue diagnosis in unresolved miliary patterns, early molecular profiling in lung adenocarcinoma, and the potential for durable exceptional responses with osimertinib in EGFR-mutated NSCLC.

title: Machine Learning-driven Prognostic Stratification in Metastatic Breast Cancer Using Dynamic 18F-FDG PET/CT: A Multidimensional Study Integrating Pathomics and Plasma Proteomics.
abstract: RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: Existing baseline-dependent metastatic breast cancer (MBC) prognostic systems remain limited in capturing tumor evolution under therapeutic pressure. We aimed to develop a dynamic 18F-FDG PET/CT-derived machine learning prognostic model and systematically explore its biological rationale using pathomics and proteomics. MATERIALS AND METHODS: PET metabolic and dynamic biomarkers were extracted from serial baseline and post-treatment 18F-FDG PET/CT images of 112 retrospectively included MBC patients. Independent prognostic biomarkers were identified using Cox regression. Prognostic models were constructed through multiple machine learning algorithms, with interpretability provided by SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP). Pathomics (n = 45) and plasma proteomics (n = 48) analyses were performed to characterize risk-associated biological features. RESULTS: Post-treatment metabolic (SUVmax2) and dynamic (ΔSULmax) PET biomarkers emerged as independent prognostic factors for progression-free survival. The final random survival forest model, termed the dynamic PET/CT-based MBC (dPMBC) prognostic model, achieved favorable prognostic stratification, yielding area under the curve values of 0.881 and 0.807 in the training and testing cohorts, respectively. SHAP identified SUVmax2 as the most influential predictive feature. Pathomics revealed distinct morphological evolution in high-risk patients, characterized by extracellular matrix remodeling and nuclear atypia. Plasma proteomics highlighted GART-centric metabolic reprogramming and immune-related alterations involving HLA-C and STAT1 within this high-risk group. CONCLUSION: The dPMBC prognostic model, integrating dynamic PET biomarkers, demonstrates promising predictive performance and biological interpretability. It enables early identification of high-risk patients during first-line therapy, supporting closer monitoring and timely individualized treatment adjustment. Pathomics and proteomics further provide biological insights into PET/CT-derived risk stratification in MBC.

title: Prognosticating Factors in PET CT and MRI of Cervical Cancer Treated With Chemoradiotherapy.
abstract: PURPOSE: We aim to evaluate the functional and anatomical imaging characteristics of locally advanced cervical cancer (LACC) to identify potential prognosticating imaging biomarkers in the context of chemoradiotherapy treatment (CRT). METHOD: This retrospective review analysed patient data over a period of seven years. Patients with locally advanced cervical cancer who have undergone FDG PET CT and MRI were identified through Report Analytics. Patients with LACC who have undergone chemoradiotherapy were identified through review of the electronic records. Pre and post-treatment imaging were analysed and compared. The patients were dichotomised into complete metabolic responders (CMR) and non-complete metabolic responders (N-CMR) as per European Organisation for Research and Treatment of Cancer (EORTC) criteria. Imaging parameters in PET CT and MRI including SUV max, SUV mean, total lesion glycolysis (TLG), lesion metabolic tumour volume (MTV), apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) minimum were examined. Kaplan-Meier analysis was used to evaluate differences in overall survival (OS) and disease-free survival (DFS) between the CMR and N-CMR groups. Pearson's correlation and Fischer's exact test were used to evaluate the potential prognosticating value of the PET CT and MRI imaging parameters as predictors of metabolic response to CRT. RESULTS: A total of 159 FDG PET CT scans were conducted in the 7-year period, of which there were 61 individual patients identified for inclusion into the present study. The average imaging follow-up for the patients included between 2019 and 2024 was 63.3 months, and chemoradiotherapy follow-up was 62.9 months. The patients were dichotomized into CMR and N-CMR groups. There is a statistically significant difference in overall survival, with 1 mortality (5%) in the CMR group vs. 19 mortality (70%) in the N-CMR group (p = 0.0001). However, no statistically significant difference in follow-up 87.1 months vs. 57.1 months (p = 0.20). In the overall cervical cancer cohort as well as the squamous cell carcinoma subgroup (n = 32), the comparison of CMR and N-CMR groups revealed a statistically significant difference in the following FDG PET imaging parameters: SUV max, SUV mean, ADC minimum and MTV. The CMR group has tumours with higher SUV max and SUV mean (difference of 7.5 and 5.1 respectively) and smaller MTV (difference of 20.1 cm3)

title: Characterisation and degradation of microplastic by Microbacterium aurantiacum isolated from biofloc in white shrimp aquaculture closed system.
mesh: Animals; Microplastics; Aquaculture; Biodegradation, Environmental; Microbacterium; Penaeidae; Flocculation; Phylogeny; Polystyrenes
abstract: This study pioneers the investigation of a novel bacteria isolated from the biofloc of a recirculating aquaculture system (RAS) for its role as a microplastic degrader. A targeted bioflocculant-producing strain was isolated and identified as Microbacterium aurantiacum (formerly known as Microbacterium chocolatum DSM12507) by phenotypic and genotypic analysis. This strain showed a good flocculation rate (95% in a kaolin test), confirming its capacity as a bioflocculant. To evaluate the performance in the degradation of microplastics (polypropylene (PP), polyethylene (PE) and polystyrene (PS), the Bushnell-Haas (BH) medium with microplastics as carbon source was used. A first screening after 14 days showed clear zones on the agar plates (S1), indicating the release of extracellular enzymes capable of depolymerizing plastic polymers. The results of quantitative gravimetric analysis after 50 days of incubation showed a significant weight loss in all microplastics: 9.2% (PP), 8.9% (PE) and 8.8% (PS), indicating that the microplastic was degraded. This biodegradation was further confirmed by remarkable structural and chemical changes visible on the sample images by spectroscopy analysis. These results suggest that bioflocs from shrimp farming not only represent an unexpected reservoir of bacteria with multiple functions, but can also contribute to environmental control through natural bioremediation. This study has highlighted the identified bioflocculant-producing bacteria, M. aurantiacum as a promising natural agent for the bioremediation of ubiquitous microplastic pollution, transforming a by-product of aquaculture into a potential solution to an environmental crisis.

title: Running tracks abrasion as a source of microplastics pollution: a long jump sandpit case study.
abstract: Modern running tracks and football fields are covered with synthetic surfaces made of polyurethane and rubber blends with an admixture of various materials. We collected sand samples from the long jump sandpits of six elementary school and university sports facilities and examined microplastics (MPs) originating from synthetic surfaces. Optical microscopy and FTIR methods were used for identification and quantification of MP particles. The spreading of MP particles was the highest in the university athletic stadium. Total MP content in the examined sand samples is in the range from 3 to 104 per 10 g of sand sample with a mean of 24 ± 17 particles per 10 g sand sample. We propose a methodology for studying microplastics in sport facilities based on collection of sand samples from the long jump sandpits. The advantage of this method is that sand is a relatively easy sampling medium for the study of MP pollution. The occurrence of microplastic particles in the sand could provide a baseline for MP pollution studies and may signal the need for appropriate surface maintenance and actions for reduction of MP pollution at its source. This study also stresses the need for appropriate management of the sand temporally removed from the long jump sandpits in order to prevent further MP pollution.

title: External validation of the SNAPP score for hepatocellular carcinoma recurrence after living donor liver transplantation.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Binary morphologic criteria cannot capture biologic heterogeneity among living donor liver transplantation (LDLT) recipients. SNAPP score (tumor size, number, AFP, PIVKA-II, PET/CT) yields a graded recurrence-risk estimate but lacks independent validation. We externally validated SNAPP for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) recurrence after LDLT. METHODS: SNAPP was applied without refitting in 230 LDLT recipients with HCC at two Korean centers and benchmarked against Milan, French-AFP, Metroticket 2.0, MoRAL, RETREAT, and three LDLT-derived selection systems (Kyoto, Medanta LDLT, and National Cancer Center Korea). Discrimination, calibration, Brier score, and reclassification were assessed using IPCW-weighted methods with bootstrap 95% CIs. RESULTS: Among 230 patients (median follow-up, 91.5 mo), 49 (21.3%) recurred. SNAPP achieved discrimination comparable to the best pretransplant tool, MoRAL (Harrell C-index, 0.756; 95% CI, 0.690-0.821), and exceeded Milan (0.503; Holm-adjusted p=0.01). Discrimination was numerically higher than Metroticket 2.0 (0.605) and three LDLT-derived systems (C-index difference, 0.10-0.15), but none of these differences survived correction for multiplicity (Holm-adjusted p=0.24). RETREAT, a posttransplant benchmark, reached 0.807. Calibration-in-the-large was -0.068; slope, 0.59 (95% CI, 0.43-0.77). Within Milan-eligible patients (n=217), SNAPP resolved a monotonic, approximately 5.9-fold gradient in 5-year cumulative recurrence (11.9%, 48.8%, 70.0%). Reclassification favored SNAPP over Milan, French-AFP, and Metroticket 2.0; the center-adjusted hazard ratio per point 1.79 (95% CI, 1.51-2.14). CONCLUSIONS: SNAPP showed discrimination comparable to MoRAL and exceeded Milan, with numerically higher but not definitively superior discrimination compared with Metroticket 2.0, French-AFP, and three LDLT-specific selection systems, while resolving biologic heterogeneity within Milan-eligible candidates using only pretransplant variables. With near-zero calibration-in-the-large but a slope below unity, SNAPP supports risk stratification at listing, though individualized probability estimates require recalibration.

title: Patterns of Care, Resource Disparities, and Professional Perceptions in Neuroendocrine Tumors in Mexico: A Nationwide Survey of Medical Oncologists.
mesh: Humans; Neuroendocrine Tumors; Mexico; Oncologists; Surveys and Questionnaires; Male; Healthcare Disparities; Practice Patterns, Physicians'; Female
abstract: PURPOSE: Neuroendocrine tumors (NETs) require accurate pathology, functional imaging, targeted therapies, and multidisciplinary care. We described NET care patterns and resource availability among Mexican medical oncologists in public and private settings. METHODS: We conducted a nationwide survey of Mexican medical oncologists. The questionnaire assessed NET caseload, perception of pathology report completeness, use of biomarkers and echocardiography, access to multidisciplinary teams (MDTs) and interventional radiology (IR), availability of nuclear medicine studies and systemic therapies, and management in key clinical scenarios. For oncologists working in both sectors, responses were reshaped into a long format, yielding 142 practice-specific observations (71 public, 71 private). RESULTS: One hundred oncologists responded, and 54% reported seeing fewer than five NET patients per year. Nearly 80% perceived that NET pathology reports were incomplete or incongruent, only 9.9% reported frequent MDT meetings, and IR was available in 19.7% of practices. NET-specific somatostatin receptor (SSTR) positron emission tomography was concentrated in private practice (60.6% v 19.7% public), and peptide receptor radionuclide therapy was available in 20.4% (similar for both practices). Somatostatin analogs were the most widely available systemic therapy (73.2% overall; 84.5% private v 62.0% public). Active surveillance, chemotherapy use, and post-somatostatin analogues sequencing were heterogeneous, with sector differences in first-line treatment for SSTR-positive grade 3 NETs. CONCLUSION: This first nationwide survey of Mexican oncologists highlights substantial public-private inequities in NET diagnostics, therapies, and multidisciplinary support, alongside concerns about pathology quality and low NET caseloads. Strengthening pathology practice, imaging, treatment access, MDTs, and education may help close NET care gaps in Mexico and other middle-income settings.

title: Preclinical Evaluation of B7-H3-Targeted ADC-Based Molecular Imaging in Lung and Triple-Negative Breast Cancer.
mesh: Humans; Animals; B7 Antigens; Female; Triple Negative Breast Neoplasms; Mice; Lung Neoplasms; Immunoconjugates; Molecular Imaging; Positron-Emission Tomography; Zirconium; Cell Line, Tumor; Radioisotopes; Tissue Distribution; Mice, Inbred BALB C; A549 Cells
abstract: B7-H3 is widely expressed in multiple solid tumors but shows minimal expression in normal tissues, making it an ideal target for molecular imaging; however, its systematic investigation remains limited. In this study, we utilized the clinically investigated B7-H3-targeted antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) HS-20093 to develop and evaluate a novel immuno-positron emission tomography (immuno-PET) tracer, [89Zr]Zr-DFO-HS-20093, for accurate imaging of B7-H3 expression in lung cancer and triple-negative breast cancer models. [89Zr]Zr-DFO-HS-20093 was synthesized with high radiochemical purity (98.2 ± 0.6%). Cellular uptake assays revealed significantly higher tracer uptake in A549 cells than in 4T1 cells at 1, 2, and 4 h (all P < 0.0001), which was markedly reduced by blocking with excess unlabeled antibody. Immunofluorescence revealed predominant membrane localization of B7-H3 in 4T1 cells, whereas A549 cells exhibited pronounced intracellular distribution, suggesting enhanced internalization. In tumor-bearing mice, [89Zr]Zr-DFO-HS-20093 positron emission tomography (PET)/CT enabled clear tumor visualization, with peak uptake at 24 h post-injection in both A549 and 4T1 xenografts (9.63 ± 1.97 and 7.15 ± 3.14 μCi/mL, respectively), supporting its potential for tumor imaging. Ex vivo biodistribution data corroborated the PET findings, showing significantly higher tracer uptake in A549 tumors (5.01 ± 1.19 % ID/g) than in blocked tumors (2.89 ± 0.43 % ID/g) and 4T1 tumors (1.89 ± 0.47 % ID/g) (P = 0.034 and P = 0.003, respectively). Immunohistochemical analysis of A549 xenografts showed strong B7-H3 expression (3+), whereas 4T1 tumors exhibited lower expression levels (1-2+), further confirming that B7-H3 expression patterns were consistent with the imaging results. [89Zr]Zr-DFO-HS-20093 enables sensitive immuno-PET imaging of B7-H3 and reveals tumor-type-dependent differences in B7-H3 expression and intracellular behavior.

title: Imaging response to neoadjuvant checkpoint inhibitor therapy in Merkel cell carcinoma: Association with pathologic response.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Radiographic biomarkers of response are needed to identify patients with Merkel cell carcinoma (MCC) who respond to neoadjuvant immunotherapy. We evaluated FDG-PET/CT characteristics associated with pathologic response. METHODS: Patients with stage III MCC treated with neoadjuvant immunotherapy and surgery (2021-2025) were retrospectively evaluated. Imaging response markers including standardized uptake value (SUVmax), total lesion glycolysis (TLG, g), and PET/CT tumor volume (cm3) were compared to pathologic response. RESULTS: Of 13 patients, 3 (23%) achieved pathologic complete response (no viable tumor), 4 (31%) achieved major response (<10% viable tumor), and 6 (46%) achieved partial/no response (>10% viable tumor). Among patients with pre- and post-neoadjuvant immunotherapy imaging (n = 7), greater reductions in SUVmax and PET/CT tumor volume were observed in complete responders; none achieved statistical significance. CONCLUSIONS: These preliminary findings highlight the need for larger prospective studies evaluating radiographic biomarkers of treatment response in MCC.

title: Beyond particle counts: Mass-based assessment reshapes ecological risk evaluation of estuarine microplastics.
abstract: This study investigates microplastic (MP) pollution in surface water and sediments of Xiamen and the Jiulong River estuary using laser direct infrared (LDIR) imaging, focusing on small-sized particles (20-500 μm). MP distribution and potential ecological risks were evaluated using number and estimated mass abundance together with the pollution load index (PLI), polymer hazard index (PHI), potential ecological risk index (PERI) and multi-scenario risk quotient (RQ). MPs were detected at all sites, with observed abundances varying among sites. In surface water, mean abundances were 518.4 ± 496.8 items L-1 and 125.1 ± 112.1 μg L-1, while sediments contained 54.8 ± 36.6 items g-1 and 27.5 ± 24.4 μg g-1. Particles <100 μm dominated all samples. A total of 18 polymer types were identified in water, primarily polypropylene (PP), whereas 19 polymer types occurred in sediments, dominated by polyethylene (PE) and PP. No significant correlation between number and mass abundances was observed in surface water, but a significant positive relationship was found in sediments. Risk assessment indicated low pollution (PLI, Class I) but elevated potential ecological risks (PHI, Class IV; PERI, Class V), driven mainly by polyurethane, polyvinyl chloride and polyacrylamide. Multi-scenario RQ analysis further showed that risk interpretation varied with MP concentration metrics and ecological effect thresholds. These findings demonstrate the value of integrating number- and estimated mass-based metrics and multiple risk assessment approaches for a more robust interpretation of MP pollution and ecological risk.

title: Impact of reduced scan extent on tumor detection in 68Ga-PSMA PET/CT for biochemical recurrence of prostate cancer.
mesh: Humans; Male; Positron Emission Tomography Computed Tomography; Prostatic Neoplasms; Gallium Radioisotopes; Retrospective Studies; Gallium Isotopes; Neoplasm Recurrence, Local; Aged; Edetic Acid; Middle Aged; Oligopeptides; Radiopharmaceuticals; Aged, 80 and over; Prostate-Specific Antigen; Whole Body Imaging
abstract: BACKGROUND: PSMA PET/CT plays an important role in biochemically recurrent prostate cancer (BCR-PCa). In general, PET/CT is performed as a limited or true whole-body examination. The majority of PET/CT scanners operate by measuring several bed positions or continuous motion with a limited axial field of view (FOV). Shortening the scan area thus results in a time saving, with unknown information loss regarding the detection of tumor manifestations. METHODOLOGY: This retrospective single-center study included 200 patients with BCR-PCa after initial curative therapy who underwent a 68Ga-PSMA-PET/CT scan from vertex to toe (true whole-body). Using retrospective subdivision into hypothetical partial body measurement protocols, the undetected tumor manifestations were examined. Classic PET/CT protocols were used: vertex to mid-thigh, skull base to mid-thigh, as well as CT-equivalent examination areas: chest/abdomen/pelvis (CAP), abdomen/pelvis (AP) and pelvis. RESULTS: Of 200 patients with a median PSA of 1.1 ng/mL, 128 (64%) showed at least one structural correlate of BCR-PCa in the true whole-body scan. The overall detection rate did not change for limited classic PET-protocols, or CAP measurements. CAP scans would not have detected all tumor manifestations in 16 patients (8%) and not all tumor-affected organ systems in six patients (3%), AP scans in 41 patients (21%) and 18 patients (9%), pelvic scans in 61 patients (31%) and 37 patients (19%), respectively. PSA may contribute to the prospective restriction of the scan area. Patients with PSA ≤ 0.75 ng/mL showed no diagnostic gain from whole-body imaging. This means that in 45% of patients in our cohort, a limitation to CAP scan would have been possible without losing information. CONCLUSIONS: For a resource-saving use of routine PSMA-PET/CT, a scan from the vertex to the mid-thigh seems sufficient for detecting relevant metastases. For patients with low PSA levels, a more focused protocol that includes only the CAP region can be considered.

title: Combined toxic effects of polyethylene microplastics (PE-MPs) and 4-nonylphenol on the common carp (Cyprinus carpio) juvenile: multi-biomarker approach.
mesh: Animals; Carps; Microplastics; Water Pollutants, Chemical; Biomarkers; Polyethylene; Phenols
abstract: There is inadequate knowledge of the cumulative impact of exposure to 4-nonylphenol (4-NP) and polyethylene microplastics (PE-MPs), and in particular of whether their joint action departs from additivity. The objective of this study was to determine and formally compare the single and combined effects of 4-NP and PE-MPs on multiple biomarkers in juvenile Cyprinus carpio. Fish were assigned to a fully crossed 2 × 2 factorial design comprising a control group and three treated groups receiving 10 mg/L PE-MPs, 200 µg/L 4-NP, or their binary mixture, for a two-week exposure period followed by a two-week depuration period. Because the four groups constitute a factorial arrangement, data were analysed by two-way ANOVA with a PE-MP × 4-NP interaction term, and departures from additivity were quantified against both effect-addition and independent-action null models.Both contaminants significantly suppressed antioxidant enzyme activity (SOD, CAT, GPx), suppressed neurological markers (AChE, MAO, NO), and elevated pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-1β, IL-6), DNA strand breakage and erythrocyte apoptosis (all P < 0.05). The PE-MP × 4-NP interaction was significant at nine of ten endpoints, but its direction depended on the biological process examined. Suppression of CAT, SOD and GPx and induction of apoptosis were greater than additive, whereas inhibition of AChE, MAO and NO and elevation of IL-1β and IL-6 were less than additive; DNA strand breakage showed no significant interaction. All departures from additivity were below the two-fold threshold conventionally required to denote toxicologically meaningful synergism, so the joint action is best described as approximately additive with endpoint-specific modulation rather than as broadly synergistic.A two-week depuration period abolished the antagonistic interactions at cholinergic and monoaminergic endpoints and returned DNA strand breakage in the single-contaminant groups to control values, but did not restore antioxidant enzyme activity, resolve cytokine elevation, or reverse apoptosis, which remained more than five-fold above control in the mixture group. title: Primary Intraparenchymal Solitary Malignant Melanoma of the Brain Without Dural Attachment: A Rare Case With Local Recurrence.
abstract: Malignant melanoma is a neoplasm arising from the malignant transformation of melanocytes. These cells are derived from the neural crest and are found predominantly in the skin, but also in mucous membranes, the uveal tract of the eye, the leptomeninges, and other sites. A 39-year-old previously healthy male presented with a holocranial headache for two months and a single episode of a focal seizure involving his left arm. Neurological exam revealed left-sided pronator drift and gross papilledema. Contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (CE-MRI) of the brain revealed a large (4.8 x 3.9 cm) heterogeneously enhancing lesion in the right parieto-occipital region with marked perilesional edema, with the provisional diagnosis of a high-grade lesion. Complete metastatic work-up, including computerized tomography (CT) of the chest and abdomen and positron emission tomography (PET), revealed no primary lesion; hence, the lesion was planned for excision. Gross total excision (GTE) was achieved, and histopathological examination (HPE) of the resected specimen confirmed malignant melanoma. Recurrence was noted 11 months later with an even bigger lesion (6.0 x 5.0 cm) on CE-MRI, and the patient succumbed to death 45 days later under the care of oncology for adjuvant chemotherapy. Primary intracerebral malignant melanomas are extremely rare tumours of the CNS. Despite surgical and chemotherapeutic treatment options, these tumours are a clinical ordeal due to their aggressive behaviour and explosive growth rate. The primary existence of melanoma intracerebrally is an oncologic enigma and needs to be included in the differential diagnosis of primary brain lesions.

title: Characterization of single and mixed microplastics in environmental matrices using Rock-Eval® pyrolysis.
abstract: Microplastics (MPs) are widespread environmental contaminants, but their rapid detection and characterization in complex matrices remain challenging. This study evaluated Rock-Eval pyrolysis as a rapid screening and semiquantitative technique for polyethylene (PE), polypropylene (PP), and polystyrene (PS) in sand, soil, and river sediment. Individual polymers were spiked into each matrix at 0.5-4 wt%, while binary (PE + PP) and ternary (PE + PP + PS) mixtures were prepared to simulate the thermal behavior of mixed polymers. Responses were evaluated using Total HC, Tmax, T10, T90, thermal degradation interval (ΔT), hydrogen index (HI), and oxygen index (OI). Total HC increased systematically with polymer loading, with R2 > 0.90 for all the polymer-matrix combinations except PS in soil. Replicate analyses at 2 wt% produced average RSDs of 11.66% for total HC and 0.40% for Tmax, providing an initial assessment of repeatability. PE and PP exhibited more matrix-dependent Tmax values, whereas PS maintained a comparatively stable Tmax of 396 °C-403 °C. Soil produced lower peak temperatures, broader hydrocarbon-release intervals, lower hydrogen indices, and higher oxygen indices than sand, reflecting contributions from indigenous organic matter. Sediments also broadened the PE and PP thermal profiles. Binary and ternary mixtures generated total HC responses approximately 23% and 72% higher, respectively, than composition-weighted values derived from the individual polymers. The ternary mixture also exhibited a broader, partially resolved bimodal S2 profile, indicating increased thermal complexity and potential non-additive behavior. These results demonstrate the proof-of-concept potential of Rock-Eval® pyrolysis for rapid MP screening and characterization while highlighting the importance of matrix and mixed-polymer effects.

title: Novel Imaging Techniques Prior to Surgical Management of Invasive Bladder Cancer: A Systematic Review.
mesh: Humans; Magnetic Resonance Imaging; Neoplasm Invasiveness; Neoplasm Staging; Sensitivity and Specificity; Urinary Bladder Neoplasms
abstract: PURPOSE OF REVIEW: To assess the diagnostic accuracy of novel imaging modalities in working up invasive bladder cancer prior to surgical management and their potential role in guiding treatment decisions. RECENT FINDINGS: Multiple new imaging modalities, including VI-RADS and Biparametric MRI have been developed to better guide management of invasive bladder cancer. There lacks a comprehensive review of these modalities and their diagnostic performance. We performed a systematic review following PRISMA guidelines. PubMed, Embase, and Scopus were searched through 2025. Studies reporting sensitivity and specificity of novel imaging for muscle invasion detection or nodal staging were included. Quality assessment used the QUADAS 2 tool. Thirty three studies encompassing 4,689 patients were included. Twenty three studies evaluated the Vesical Imaging Reporting and Data System for muscle invasion detection, achieving median sensitivity of 94% and specificity of 82% at a threshold of three or greater and 84% and 92%, respectively, at four or greater. Nine studies assessed positron emission tomography for nodal staging, with fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/computed tomography demonstrating superior sensitivity (23 to 81%) compared to conventional computed tomography (13 to 47%). Fibroblast activation protein inhibitor tracers showed the highest sensitivity (82 to 100%) with specificity of 82 to 90%. One radiomics study achieved 73% sensitivity and 84% specificity for lymph node detection. Novel imaging modalities demonstrate promising diagnostic accuracy for bladder cancer staging. The Vesical Imaging Reporting and Data System provides reliable muscle invasion assessment with threshold dependent performance. Positron emission tomography with fibroblast activation protein inhibitor tracers substantially improves nodal staging over conventional computed tomography. Integration of these modalities may optimize patient management, including use or omission of neoadjuvant therapy and consideration for organ sparing approaches. Prospective multicenter validation is needed.
